title: A Worm Lives With Its Tail in 80°C Water, Its Head in Cool Sea
subject: Pompeii worm

scenes.text: This worm lives in water hot enough to hurt. Its head stays cool.
It lives in tubes on deep sea vent chimneys, about 2,500 meters down.
Its tail sits in water that can reach 80 degrees Celsius.
scenes.keywords: hydrothermal vent hot water deep sea

scenes.text: Its head pokes out into cool seawater at the tube's mouth.
And its back is covered in a grey fuzz of bacteria, which may work like a thermal blanket.
So the worm stays cool in a place hot enough to hurt.

description:
A Pompeii worm lives with its tail in water that can reach 80 degrees Celsius and its head in cool seawater.
Its back is covered in a fuzz of bacteria that may act as a thermal blanket.
Could you stand a bath at 80 degrees?
first_comment: The fuzz can be up to a centimeter thick, and the bacteria feed on sugars the worm secretes. Which extreme animal should we cover next?
